name: Mount Vaea
variants: A 472 m climb above Apia to Robert Louis Stevenson's grave, with views east over the Pacific.
An easy hour's walk up a 472 m summit above Apia to Stevenson's grave and a Pacific view.
The hilltop grave of Robert Louis Stevenson, 472 m above Apia, reached on an easy walk of about an hour.

name: Robert Louis Stevenson Museum
variants: Villa Vailima, the house Stevenson built in 1891 and lived in until his death, now a museum south of Apia.
Stevenson's restored home, Villa Vailima, where he wrote The Bottle Imp, 5 km south of Apia.
The 1891 villa where Robert Louis Stevenson spent his last years, furnished as he lived in it.

name: Museum of Samoa
variants: Samoa's national museum in a century-old German school, with Lapita pottery, adzes and tattoo history.
A colonial-era school at Malifa housing Lapita pottery, stone adzes, old photographs and Samoan birds.
The national museum, in a German-built school at Malifa, covering Lapita pottery, tattooing and old photographs.

name: Palolo Deep Marine Reserve
variants: A marine reserve at Vaiala Beach where snorkellers swim past the reef edge to find turtles and reef sharks.
Snorkelling reserve at Vaiala Beach, east of Apia, best on a rising tide, with occasional turtles.
Apia's underwater park at Vaiala Beach, with snorkel hire on site and blacktip reef sharks further out.

name: Papase'ea Sliding Rocks
variants: A natural water slide over falls into a pool, 6 km south-west of Apia, best in the rainy season.
Slide down mossy rock into a pool below the falls, a village-run stop 6 km south-west of Apia.
A natural rock slide and plunge pool near Apia that suits all ages, running best in the rainy season.

name: Samoa Cultural Village
variants: A Beach Road cultural centre in Apia with songs, dances, umu cooking, kava ceremonies and craft workshops.
Apia centre showing Samoan customs through dance, umu cooking, a kava ceremony and crafts.
Hands-on introduction to Samoan customs on Beach Road, Apia, with song, dance, kava and workshops.

name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
variants: Apia's Catholic cathedral, finished in the mid-19th century and rebuilt after the 2009 earthquake.
A cupola-topped Catholic cathedral in Apia, reopened in 2014 after earthquake repairs and extension.
One of Apia's largest buildings, a 19th-century cathedral renovated and extended after the 2009 earthquake.

name: Papapapai-tai Falls
variants: Samoa's tallest waterfall, a roughly 100 m drop seen from a viewing area on the Cross Island Road.
A roughly 100 m plunge, the tallest waterfall in Samoa, viewed from a roadside lookout.
Viewing area on the Cross Island Road for Samoa's tallest waterfall, which falls about 100 m.

name: Lake Lanoto'o National Park
variants: A 470 ha park in central Upolu around three crater lakes, with a goldfish-filled lake and rare swamp forest.
Ramsar-listed crater lakes in Upolu's interior, reached by 4WD and a short walk from the Cross Island Road.
Three volcanic crater lakes and swamp forest in Upolu's highlands, protected since 2003.

name: Piula Cave Pool
variants: A spring-fed freshwater pool by the sea beneath a Methodist chapel, 26 km east of Apia.
Swim in a natural freshwater pool under the chapel at Piula, reached down steps through the college wall.
Cave pool beside the sea at Piula, entered through a painted stone wall; closed on Sundays.

name: Return to Paradise Beach
variants: A beach near Lefaga on the south-west coast where the 1953 film Return to Paradise, with Gary Cooper, was shot.
Lefaga's south-west coast beach, the setting for the 1953 Gary Cooper film Return to Paradise.
A beach on Upolu's south-west coast near Lefaga, known as the location of a 1953 Hollywood film.

name: Manono Island
variants: A car-free island 20 minutes by boat off Upolu's western tip, with four villages and a footpath round the coast.
Four villages, beach fales and a coastal footpath on a roadless island in the Apolima Strait.
Car-free island in the Apolima Strait where you can walk the coast past villages and a prehistoric mound.

name: Namu'a Island
variants: A secluded island within the reef off Upolu's eastern tip, with beach fales and turtles often seen on the boat.
Reef-ringed island off Upolu's east, reached by a short boat ride from near Lalomanu Beach.
Quiet island off Upolu's eastern tip with beach fales, where turtles often appear on the short boat trip.

name: O Le Pupu-Pu'e National Park
variants: Samoa's oldest national park, from Mount Fito to a rugged lava coast, with the Ma Tree and Pe'ape'a Cave.
A 5019 ha park on Upolu's south with rainforest trails, lava cliffs and a 700 m walk to a giant buttressed tree.
Established in 1978, this park runs from upland forest to a lava coast with a six-hour walk to Pe'ape'a Cave.

name: Togitogiga Falls
variants: Cascades and cool swimming holes inside O Le Pupu-Pu'e National Park, with changing rooms, best in the wet season.
Gentle falls linked by swimming waterholes in O Le Pupu-Pu'e National Park, with toilets and parking.
A series of small waterfalls and cool pools for swimming on Upolu's south coast.

name: To Sua Ocean Trench
variants: A 30 m deep seawater swimming hole in a collapsed lava tube near Lotofaga, reached by a long wooden ladder.
A turquoise swimming hole in a collapsed lava tube, entered by ladder, on Upolu's south coast.
Climb down a wooden ladder into a deep, turquoise ocean-fed pool in the lava field.

name: Lalomanu Beach
variants: A white-sand beach on Upolu's south-east coast looking out to small islands, with beach fales and boats to Namua.
Beach fales line this south-east Upolu beach, facing the small Aleipata islands.
Upolu's south-east beach village, with beach fales, a dive shop and views of idyllic small islands.

name: Alofaaga Blowholes
variants: Lava-tube blowholes by Taga village where waves shoot fountains from the clifftop rock every few seconds.
Waves force water up lava tubes at Taga on Savai'i's south-west coast, spraying fountains every few seconds.
Clifftop blowholes at Taga where ocean surges burst through lava tubes in fountains.

name: Saleaula Lava Field
variants: Lava field from the 1905-11 Matavanu eruptions that buried two villages, with guided visits to surviving churches.
A lava field over a century old covering two villages, with a guided walk to ruined churches and the Virgin's Grave.
Guided visits to the lava that buried Sale'aula, including two churches that escaped destruction.

name: Pulemelei Mound
variants: The largest and most ancient human-made structure in the Samoan Islands, a 12 m tall mound in east Savai'i.
A 12 m tall stepped mound, 60 m by 50 m at its base, in Letolo Plantation, near Olemoe Falls.
Ancient mound in Letolo Plantation, also called Tia Seu, the biggest ancient structure in Samoa.

name: Afu Aau Falls
variants: A spring-fed jungle waterfall on Savai'i's south coast, with a swimming hole a short walk from the entrance fale.
Also called Olemoe Falls, a waterfall and 3 m deep spring-fed pool reached on a short jungle trail.
South-coast waterfall on Savai'i with a deep waterhole for swimming in the dry season.

name: Mount Matavanu
variants: The volcano whose 1905-11 eruptions covered much of north Savai'i in lava, reached by a long walk from Paia.
A three-hour walk from Paia village through barren lava fields to the Matavanu crater, a geological heritage site.
Crater of the volcano behind Savai'i's lava fields, reached on a guided walk across a moonscape.

name: Falealupo Rainforest Preserve
variants: Village-run rainforest preserve on Savai'i's north-west tip, with a 24 m canopy bridge to a platform in a 230-year-old banyan.
A canopy bridge nearly 10 m above the forest floor, leading to a platform in an old banyan.
Customary-owned forest on Savai'i's north-west peninsula, with a canopy walk strung between large trees.

name: Tafua Peninsula Rainforest Preserve
variants: Rainforest preserve on Savai'i's south-east peninsula, good for birdwatching, with a walk up to a volcanic crater.
South-east Savai'i peninsula with rainforest, excellent birdwatching and a climb to the Mauga Tafua crater.
Forest and birdlife on the Tafua Peninsula, with a walk to the volcanic crater that dominates it.

name: Paia Dwarfs Cave
variants: A lava tube over a kilometre long near Paia village, explored with a local guide, said in legend to be home to dwarves.
Lava tube near Paia, crossing underground rivers, entered only with a village guide.
Legend says dwarves live in this lava tube over a kilometre long, which needs a local guide.
